To: Lander Structures IPT Lead
From: C. Ortega, FEA
Subject: Quick look — structural M&S credibility for avionics tray bracket (Abaqus 2023HF3)
Date: 06 Aug 2026

Purpose and decision tie-in
- Goal is to establish whether the machined 7075-T73 avionics tray bracket (P/N LND-AV-312) can carry quasi-static ascent loads (1.8g axial, 1.2g lateral) plus random vibe (0.1 g^2/Hz @ 80–350 Hz, OA 10.1 g RMS) with positive margin at the fillet near the forward tie-down.
- The near-term decision is bracket release for machining Lot 2 with no design change; analysis must be trustworthy enough to bound stresses/strains at the two critical features we flagged in PR-1012.

Model setup and physics choices
- Abaqus/Standard 2023HF3, implicit, small-strain with geometric nonlinearity enabled in contact only (surfaces may open/slide).
- Solid tetra elements (C3D10) in body; bolt shanks are beam elements tied to hole surfaces; preload via bolt load step; nut contact modeled with surface-to-surface, penalty method, µ = 0.25 nominal.
- Material: 7075-T73 isotropic elastic-plastic, E = 71.5 GPa, ν = 0.33; bilinear kinematic plasticity with 0.2% offset yield = 365 MPa, tangent = 1.1 GPa. Temperature effects ignored (enclosure stays 18–28 C).
- Boundary: Tray rails fixed to the chassis hardpoint pattern per CAD constraint map ASM-A1; vibe PSD applied as base acceleration to the mount set; static loads scaled by mass properties from CAD R38.

Numerical behavior and mesh checks
- Three meshes around the hot fillet: 1.6M/3.2M/6.7M DOF. Peak von Mises at the fillet changed +12.1% (coarse→medium) and +3.0% (medium→fine). Medium retained for production runs; extrapolated peak change to zero size ≈ 2.6%. Reaction force imbalance <0.5% for all.
- Contact penetration averaged 3.2 µm at peak load; cutback events <5 per step after tuning penalties. Newton residuals dropped 4 orders per increment in nonlinear steps.

Algorithm and implementation confidence
- Sanity checks against NAFEMS LE10 and a thick-plate-with-corner-load closed form: tip deflection error 0.9–1.2% with same element family and formulation.
- Ran vendor-supplied patch tests (Abaqus QA set) for quadratic tets under combined bending/membrane; no spurious modes observed. Verified the 2023HF3 fix for the follower load bug (SPR 140323) present in HF1—our bolt preload results are stable across increments.

Comparison to physical data
- Subcomponent 3-point bend on a geometrically similar bracket coupon (same fillet radius and thickness) at Test Lab 17, Instron 5985, room temp, preload added via torque-to-tension. Two gages at the fillet, one at the web.
- FE vs test: midspan strain within 6%; fillet gage within 9% at 80% of limit load; slope change at onset of plasticity captured within 10 MPa effective stress when we use µ = 0.22 instead of 0.25. We did not tune E; friction adjustment only.

Inputs pedigree
- Material data from MMPDS-17 7075-T73 plate (1.0–1.5 in); our stock certs match within 2.3% on E from ultrasonic NDI correlations.
- Vibe PSD from TVAC-vibe rehearsal log 05/19/26, averaged across two runs; co-quantized to 1/6 octave for model input. Bolt torque limits per NASM1312-31, translated to preload with k = 0.18 (scatter addressed below).

Uncertainty and variability treatment
- 200-run Monte Carlo (Latin hypercube) on µ ∈ [0.15, 0.35], preload ±15%, E ±3%, fillet radius ±0.15 mm machining tolerance.
- 95th percentile peak von Mises at the fillet: 312 MPa; 99th percentile: 334 MPa. Plastic strain remains <0.15% in 97% of samples. Dominant contributor is preload variability.
- Local sensitivity (finite-difference) near nominal: dσ/dP_bolt ≈ 0.62 MPa/N; friction has nonlinear effect near 0.2–0.3 with sign change in slip transition. Sobol first-order indices (surrogate GP): preload 0.47, friction 0.28, radius 0.18, E 0.05.

People, tools, and reproducibility
- Analyst quals: NAFEMS PSE (Structures) passed 2024; 8 yrs Abaqus/Standard, 3 yrs MSC Nastran nonlinear.
- All scripts and .cae in GitLab repo av-bracket-fea, tag v0.6.4; Abaqus kernel/CAE versions recorded in run logs; mesh seeds generated by Python 3.10 environment pinned via conda-lock file; Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. Random seeds for UQ archived; results reproduced on a second workstation within numerical noise.

Limitations worth noting
- No micro-slip wear modeling; constant µ used. Adhesive under EMI gasket omitted; fastener head compliance simplified via beam head offsets. Thermal preload relaxation not included. Random vibe linearized about preloaded state (no contact opening in PSD run).

Bottom line
- With the current modeling choices and evidence above, I judge the analysis adequate to green-light Lot 2 machining. We retain ~50 MPa headroom to yield at the critical fillet at the 95th percentile outcome; spot plasticity, if it occurs, is predicted to be sub-0.2% and non-propagating. I recommend keeping the µ and preload scatter in the acceptance test plan to bound as-built performance.
